Hi Karthik,

We're kicking off the vendor master setup for Acme Supplies — we have a US-registered subsidiary (Acme Supplies, Inc., EIN: 12-3456789) and an EU billing entity (Acme Supplies Europe B.V.). The immediate need is to receive POs for recurring hardware orders from Redwood's US team while invoices should (where applicable) route to our EU AP team for VAT handling.

High-level asks:
- Create a primary vendor master for the US legal entity with PO routing to procure@acme-supplies.com.
- Add a secondary remit/billing contact for the EU entity (billing@acme-eu.com) so invoices can be routed there as needed.
- We will attach W-9 and Certificate of Incorporation to confirm the registered name and address.

Attachments: W-9_AcmeSupplies_2027.pdf; Certificate_of_Incorporation_AcmeSupplies.pdf

Can you confirm what additional fields your AP and master-data team need (registered address format, DBA fields, tax jurisdiction)? Also flag if PO destination needs to be different from invoice remit.

Thanks — happy to set a 20-min call if that's easier.

Hi Jia — thanks for the quick intro and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (AP ops) and Laura (Legal) to confirm a couple of edge cases. Below is the vendor master checklist we need to finalize:

Required for master creation (please reply inline):
1) Legal name (exact as on tax docs) — appears to be "Acme Supplies, Inc." for US entity. Confirm capitalization/punctuation.
2) Registered (legal) address for US entity — street, city, state, ZIP.
3) Remit/billing address for EU entity (if different) + AP contact name/email.
4) Tax identifier(s): US EIN and EU VAT number (if applicable).
5) Preferred PO recipient (email) and PO acknowledgement workflow (auto-accept vs manual).
6) Banking rails for cross-border payments (ACH vs SWIFT/EFT) — Marissa will advise.
7) Any operating DBAs or alternate legal names to surface in the master record.
8) Who is authorized to sign invoices/credit memos (name + title).

Marissa — for cross-border remit, please confirm whether we should set up a single vendor with two remit contacts (US invoices stay with US remit; EU invoices route to billing@acme-eu.com) or two separate vendor masters (one per legal entity). Laura — I see a registered-address mismatch in the certificate vs the billing address in the PDF header; please confirm whether Record -> secondary name proofing is required.

If you can return answers to items 1–4 and confirm the preferred PO email, I can draft the master record and generate a PO fallback plan (if PO-to-invoice mismatch occurs) so we don't lose PO-led shipments.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Manager, Supplier Onboarding
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Karthik / Jia — quick AP notes: 
- If the US entity has an EIN (12-3456789) we'll process US invoices via ACH to a US bank account. If payments need to flow to the EU entity, we need a separate master pointing to the EU bank details.
- For immediate fulfillment tied to POs raised by our US buyers, recommend creating one vendor master for the US legal entity (primary), with a secondary remit contact for the EU billing address. That lets POs map to the US master_id while invoices can be routed to EU AP and flagged for VAT processing.
- Please provide bank country and currency expectations. If the bank is outside the US, we'll default to wire (SWIFT) and flag for FX.

Also: include a POC for invoicing disputes (name + email) and preferred invoice format (PDF attached to AP email vs EDI).

Short list for the vendor to reply with: legal name, registered US address, remit EU address, US EIN, EU VAT (if any), AP contact for EU, bank country/currency.

Thanks — Marissa
